subject: Follow-up: ZenithPay throughput baseline & connection strategy
messages:
From: Nina Patel <nina.patel@zenithpay.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Amit Rao <amit.rao@zenithpay.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap + next steps from today's latency/throughput sync

Ben / Marissa — thanks again for the call this morning. Helpful to see the baseline numbers and the options you outlined for connection reuse vs. aggressive parallelization. Quick recap from our side and a few follow-ups so we can size the POC properly: 

- Production target: 99th percentile tail latency under 180ms for single-turn payment batched lookups (median ~40ms).
- Expected sustained throughput: ~2,500 requests/min during business hours, with spikes ~8,000 requests/min during settlement windows (~10 minutes, twice a day).
- Typical request size: 150–600 tokens. Some streaming use (websocket-style receipts) for 10% of traffic — needs low-latency partial-chunk delivery.
- We can tolerate a per-tenant concurrency cap; important is predictable degradation not complete failures.

Open questions we promised to confirm:
1) Can Redwood support long-lived connection pooling (keep-alive + multiplexed HTTP/2) from a small set of EB nodes to reduce TCP churn?
2) Do you have guidance on session/connection reuse strategy for streaming requests vs short generative calls?
3) What would a ratecap proposal look like for the POC (burst window, steady-state, connection quota)?

Action for us: I attached a short spreadsheet with our traffic shape and a diagram of our current gateway topology. Please flag anything that looks off.

Best,
Nina Patel
Head of Integrations, ZenithPay
N: +1 415-555-0189

[attachment: zenithpay_poc_requirements.xlsx (xlsx, 42KB)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@zenithpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Jun 2025 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps from today's latency/throughput sync

Nina — great notes, thanks for sending. Quick answers up front then a proposed POC ratecap so we can align expectations: 

1) Long-lived connections: yes, Redwood supports persistent HTTP/1.1 keep-alive and HTTP/2 multiplexing for hosted and Dedicated. For Private we can also enable a small pool of egress nodes if you want to localize connections.

2) Streaming vs short calls: recommend connection-affinity for streams (pin a stream to the same backend) to avoid rehydrating KV cache repeatedly. Short generative calls benefit from shared connection pools with aggressive prefix/KV caching. Our runtime will prefer cached prefixes and route short-turn traffic to smaller model variants if configured.

3) POC ratecap proposal (initial):
   - Steady-state: 2,500 r/min (token-aware; we factor avg token length).
   - Burst window: allow 3x steady-state for 2 minutes (7,500 r/min) with token-based throttling afterwards.
   - Connection quota: 500 concurrent connections from ZenithPay's EB pool; if you want fewer connections we can gate parallel requests per-connection.
   - Streaming concurrency: reserve 50 concurrent long-lived streams with soft prioritization.

Notes: those numbers are conservative to start. We can loosen burst/connection caps as we validate hit rates in the first 2–3 days of the POC. If you expect longer bursts (e.g., 20min settlement spikes) call that out and we can size accordingly.

Next steps: 
- Marissa will follow with a short checklist for instrumentation we need (sample trace headers, example websocket handshake).
- Jonas will send a diagram for the connection topology we recommend and an initial traffic shaping policy.

Happy to hop on a quick 20-min call today to walk the spreadsheet.

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0123

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@zenithpay.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Jun 2025 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps from today's latency/throughput sync

Adding a few technical details from the infra side that will help you plan: 

- KV/prefix caching: For 150–600 token requests we typically hit local KV cache >80% if you keep session-affinity for short windows (~30s). That drastically reduces tail latency.
- Multiplexing: HTTP/2 is best when you can reuse ~50–100 connections per EB (we saw diminishing returns above that for small requests).
- Socket limits and ephemeral ports: if you front Redwood with their own EB pool, ensure ephemeral port exhaustion isn't possible — we usually recommend NAT port pools >= 8K for the POC cluster.
- Backpressure: our runtime uses token-aware throttles rather than pure QPS caps; provide us average token-per-request and peak-token bursts so we can match policy.

For streaming receipts (10% traffic): implement chunked responses where the client can reconnect with a resume token — this lets us garbage-collect KV state for inactive streams while preserving partial delivery.

Attached a quick diagram of the recommended topology and an example config snippet for the rate limiter.

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

[attachment: conn_strategy_diagram.png (png, 78KB)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@zenithpay.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Jun 2025 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps from today's latency/throughput sync

Nina — tagging on a few operational items and next steps for the POC kickoff: 

- I'll provision an ephemeral test endpoint for you to send synthetic traffic (same auth as production) so we can validate steady-state + the 2-minute burst window. Expect the endpoint by EOD tomorrow.
- Suggested initial traffic shaping policy (will post to the HubSpot deal):
   * Token-aware throttle: steady 2,500 r/min; burst to 7,500 r/min for 2 minutes with a 15s cool-down token decay.
   * Connection gate: 500 concurrent connections. If ZenithPay wants to push more concurrency without increasing TCP footprint, we recommend increasing per-connection parallelism (max in-flight requests per connection = 8).
   * Streaming pool: 50 reserved stream slots; additional streams get queued with priority for confirmed settlement flows.

Please confirm if you want us to: 
1) Lower the connection quota to 250 for the first 24 hours and increase if metrics look healthy (good for NAT-limited environments).
2) Enable HTTP/2-only mode for the EB -> Redwood path (reduces connection count but requires client support).

I'll attach the traffic generator script and link the HubSpot record when I post the shaping policy.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com
